docs.title: Admin Panel Installation Guide (cPanel + Manual .env + Terminal + /install)
docs.text: This guide is for beginners. Follow each step in order to install your Laravel Admin Panel (API backend) on cPanel shared hosting.

docs.title: 1) Create domain (cPanel → Domains)
docs.text:
1. Log in to cPanel.
  2. Open Domains.
  3. Create a new domain/subdomain:
  4. api.example.com
  5. Note the folder path created by cPanel, for example:
  6. /home/CPANELUSER/api.example.com

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Domain/subdomain api.example.com is created
  • [ ] Domain folder exists in File Manager

✅ Expected Result: domain is created and folder exists.

⚠️ Common Mistakes - Creating the domain with a typo (for example ap1.example.com). - Using the wrong folder path later in terminal commands.

docs.title: 2) Create DB + user (cPanel → MySQL Databases)
docs.text:
1. Open MySQL Databases in cPanel.
  2. Create a new database (example):
  3. example_api
  4. Create a new database user (example):
  5. example_user
  6. Add the user to the database.
  7. Grant ALL PRIVILEGES.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Database created
  • [ ] DB user created
  • [ ] User added to DB
  • [ ] ALL PRIVILEGES enabled

✅ Expected Result: DB user has full access.

⚠️ Common Mistakes - Forgetting to add user to database. - Not giving ALL PRIVILEGES. - Forgetting cPanel prefixes (actual names often look like cpuser_example_api).

docs.title: 3) Upload ZIP + unzip (cPanel → File Manager)
docs.text:
1. Open File Manager.
  2. Go to:
  3. /home/CPANELUSER/api.example.com
  4. Upload your admin panel ZIP file.
  5. Extract/unzip the file in this same folder.
  6. Confirm these items exist:
  7. artisan
  8. composer.json
  9. public/
  10. storage/
  11. bootstrap/cache/

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] ZIP uploaded
  • [ ] ZIP extracted
  • [ ] Laravel files/folders confirmed

✅ Expected Result: Laravel project files are present.

⚠️ Common Mistakes - Extracting ZIP into a subfolder (for example /api.example.com/project-name/) instead of the domain root. - Uploading incomplete project files.

docs.title: 4) Manually edit .env (before installer)
docs.text:
1. In File Manager, open .env in:
  2. /home/CPANELUSER/api.example.com/.env
  3. If .env is missing, create it by copying:
  4. .env.example → .env
  5. Fill/update these values:
APP_NAME="Your App Name"
APP_ENV=production
APP_DEBUG=false
APP_URL=https://api.example.com

DB_CONNECTION=mysql
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=3306
DB_DATABASE=YOUR_DB_NAME
DB_USERNAME=YOUR_DB_USER
DB_PASSWORD="YOUR_DB_PASS"
  1. Save the file.
  2. Make sure .env is writable by your cPanel user.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] .env exists
  • [ ] DB values are correct
  • [ ] APP_URL is https://api.example.com
  • [ ] File saved successfully

✅ Expected Result: .env has correct DB + URL values.

⚠️ Common Mistakes - Wrong DB credentials. - Leaving APP_DEBUG=true in production. - Setting APP_URL to the main website instead of API domain.

docs.title: 5) Set document root to /public (cPanel)
docs.text:
1. Go to cPanel → Domains.
  2. Click Manage for api.example.com.
  3. Set Document Root to:
/home/CPANELUSER/api.example.com/public
  1. Save changes.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Document Root updated to /public
  • [ ] Saved in cPanel successfully

✅ Expected Result: Laravel runs from /public (secure + correct).

⚠️ Common Mistakes - Keeping document root at /home/CPANELUSER/api.example.com (not secure and usually breaks routing).

docs.title: 6) Run terminal commands (cPanel → Terminal or SSH)
docs.text:
Run these commands in order.

cd /home/CPANELUSER/api.example.com
composer install --no-dev --optimize-autoloader
composer dump-autoload
php artisan key:generate
php artisan optimize:clear
php artisan storage:link
chmod -R 775 storage bootstrap/cache

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• composer dump-autoload is optional, but useful if autoload issues appear.
  • php artisan optimize:clear is optional but recommended.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] vendor/ folder created
  • [ ] No fatal permission errors
  • [ ] public/storage exists as a symlink

✅ Expected Result: - vendor/ exists - no permission errors - public/storage is a symlink

⚠️ Common Mistakes - Running commands in the wrong folder. - Composer not available in cPanel environment. - Permissions not updated for storage and bootstrap/cache.

docs.title: 7) Open /install and finish wizard
docs.text:
1. Open:
  2. https://api.example.com/install
  3. Screen 1: Requirements check (PHP extensions, permissions, storage paths).
  4. Continue to the next screen.
  5. Fill installer fields:
  6. Database details
  7. Host URL
  8. Public Site URL (if shown)
  9. Click Install.

docs.title: What the installer does
docs.text:
• Runs migrate --force
  • Runs db:seed --force only if DB is fresh/empty
  • Runs storage:link again
  • Creates lock file:
  • storage/app/installed.lock

docs.title: Finish screen should show
docs.text:
• Admin login URL
  • Login email
  • Login password

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Requirements passed
  • [ ] Install process completed
  • [ ] Credentials shown on finish screen

✅ Expected Result: install completed and admin URL shown.

⚠️ Common Mistakes - Trying to run installer before .env is correct. - Ignoring failed requirements (permissions/extensions).

docs.title: 8) Installation lock (after success)
docs.text:
After a successful install, the lock file should exist:

storage/app/installed.lock

This lock must block future access to /install.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] installed.lock exists after install
  • [ ] /install is blocked after install

✅ Expected Result: /install is blocked after install.

⚠️ Common Mistakes - Lock file missing due to write permission problems. - Custom routes/middleware accidentally leaving /install open.

docs.title: 9) Login + post setup
docs.text:
1. Open admin login URL from installer finish screen.
  2. Log in with installer credentials.
  3. Complete post-setup sections:

docs.title: A) Firebase / Google settings
docs.text:
• Upload service account JSON
  • Fill required Firebase/Google keys

docs.title: B) SMTP email settings
docs.text:
• Set SMTP host, port, username, password
  • Set encryption (tls/ssl)
  • Set From name and From email
  • Send a test email

docs.title: C) AI settings
docs.text: • Add OpenAI API key and/or Gemini API key

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Firebase configured
  • [ ] SMTP test email sent successfully
  • [ ] AI API keys saved and tested

✅ Expected Result: Firebase, Email, and AI integrations are working.

⚠️ Common Mistakes - Invalid JSON file for Firebase. - Wrong SMTP port/encryption combination. - API keys saved with extra spaces or quotes.

docs.title: 1. 500 error after document root change
docs.text:
• Confirm document root is exactly:
  • /home/CPANELUSER/api.example.com/public
  • Confirm project files are one level above public.
  • Run:
cd /home/CPANELUSER/api.example.com
php artisan optimize:clear

docs.title: 2. DB connection failed
docs.text:
• Recheck .env values:
  • DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_DATABASE, DB_USERNAME, DB_PASSWORD
  • Ensure DB user is added to DB with ALL PRIVILEGES.
  • Remember cPanel DB names often include account prefix.

docs.title: 3. Composer install failed
docs.text:
• If memory limit error appears, increase PHP/CLI memory in cPanel if available.
  • If composer command is missing, use host-provided Composer path or ask hosting support to enable Composer.

docs.title: 4. storage / bootstrap/cache not writable
docs.text:
• Re-run:
cd /home/CPANELUSER/api.example.com
chmod -R 775 storage bootstrap/cache

docs.title: 5. public/storage not working
docs.text:
• public/storage must be a symlink, not a normal folder.
  • Fix by removing wrong folder and running:
cd /home/CPANELUSER/api.example.com
php artisan storage:link

docs.title: 6. Seeder skipped (DB already has users)
docs.text:
• This is normal if database is not fresh.
  • Installer usually seeds only on a fresh/empty DB.
  • Existing users/data remain unchanged.

docs.title: 7. /install still accessible after install
docs.text:
• Check if lock file exists:
  • storage/app/installed.lock
  • If missing, verify write permissions.
  • If lock exists but page still opens, review installer middleware/route protection in your codebase.

✅ Expected Result: common issues are identified and fixed quickly.

⚠️ Common Mistakes - Changing many settings at once and not retesting step-by-step. - Not clearing cache after config fixes.

docs.title: Do I only need this website to install MegaClassify?
docs.text: No. You must also read and follow the documentation included inside the CodeCanyon ZIP package delivered with your purchase.

docs.title: I completed installation but get a 500 error. What should I check?
docs.text:
• Confirm .env values are valid
  • Check PHP version and required extensions
  • Verify file permissions for storage/ and bootstrap/cache/
  • Run cache clear commands:
php artisan optimize:clear

docs.title: Uploaded images are not visible.
docs.text:
Most commonly, the storage symlink is missing. Run:

php artisan storage:link

docs.title: Mobile/Web app cannot connect to API.
docs.text:
• Check API base URL is correct (https://apimega.megzed.com format)
  • Validate CORS configuration in backend
  • Confirm SSL certificate is valid
  • Ensure no firewall blocks API routes

docs.title: Database migration failed on production.
docs.text:
Use safe migration command:

php artisan migrate --force

Also ensure database credentials and privileges are correct.

docs.title: Support
docs.text: Need help with MegaClassify setup or troubleshooting?

docs.title: Contact Support
docs.text:
• Email: megaclassify@gmail.com
  • WhatsApp: 7032202023

docs.title: Before Contacting Support
docs.text:
Please prepare:

  • Purchase code / buyer details (masked if needed)
  • Current version/build number
  • Server environment details (OS, PHP, DB, web server)
  • Exact error message and screenshot
  • Relevant logs (storage/logs/laravel.log, web server logs)

docs.title: Common Fast Checks
docs.text:
1. Reconfirm all installation steps were followed
  2. Verify .env values
  3. Re-run:
php artisan optimize:clear
php artisan storage:link
  1. Confirm permissions on writable folders
  2. Review the CodeCanyon bundled documentation

docs.title: Support Scope
docs.text:
Support generally covers:

  • Installation guidance
  • Configuration clarification
  • Bug diagnosis and known fixes

Customization and third-party infrastructure tuning may require additional effort.

docs.title: Setup Admin Panel - Configuration
docs.text: After installation, finalize production-safe configuration.

docs.title: 1) Essential .env Configuration
docs.text:
Review and tune:

  • APP_ENV=production
  • APP_DEBUG=false
  • APP_URL=https://{{YOUR_DOMAIN}}
  • DB credentials
  • Mail credentials
  • Queue/session/cache drivers

Never commit real .env values to Git.

docs.title: 2) Queue & Cron (Recommended)
docs.text:
For better performance, configure worker/cron if package requires background jobs.

Typical scheduler cron:

* * * * * cd /home/{{CPANEL_USER}}/{{APP_PATH}} && php artisan schedule:run >> /dev/null 2>&1

docs.title: 3) Web Server Best Practices (Apache/Nginx)
docs.text:
• Enforce HTTPS
  • Enable gzip/brotli (if available)
  • Add reasonable client upload size for listing media
  • Block direct access to sensitive files (.env, .git)

Sample location protection snippet:

location ~ /\.(env|git) {
    deny all;
}

docs.title: 4) CORS/API Considerations
docs.text:
If mobile or web app cannot call API:

  • Confirm APP_URL and API base URL are correct
  • Configure allowed origins in CORS settings
  • Ensure OPTIONS preflight requests are handled
  • Validate SSL and intermediate certificates

docs.title: 5) File Permission Policy
docs.text:
Writable paths:

  • storage/
  • bootstrap/cache/

Use least-privilege settings and avoid world writable permissions.

docs.title: HTTP 500 Error
docs.text:
1. Check Laravel log:
tail -n 200 storage/logs/laravel.log
  1. Check Apache/Nginx error logs from cPanel (Metrics/Errors or domain logs)
  2. Validate PHP version/extensions
  3. Re-run:
php artisan optimize:clear

docs.title: Storage Link Issue (Images Not Loading)
docs.text:
php artisan storage:link

Ensure public/storage points to storage/app/public.

docs.title: CORS Errors
docs.text:
• Verify frontend origin is allowed
  • Clear config cache:
php artisan optimize:clear
  • Confirm reverse proxy is not stripping headers

docs.title: Permission Denied Errors
docs.text:
find /home/{{CPANEL_USER}}/{{APP_PATH}} -type f -exec chmod 644 {} \;
find /home/{{CPANEL_USER}}/{{APP_PATH}} -type d -exec chmod 755 {} \;
chmod -R 775 storage bootstrap/cache

docs.title: Migration Issues
docs.text:
php artisan migrate --force

Confirm DB user privileges (ALTER, CREATE, INDEX, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE).

docs.title: 7) Backup & Update Policy
docs.text:
Before each update:

  • Backup database
  • Backup .env
  • Backup uploaded media (storage/app/public)

After update:

composer install --no-dev -o
php artisan migrate --force
php artisan optimize:clear

docs.title: Setup Admin Panel - Prerequisite
docs.text:
Need a Faster Launch? We Can Help With Setup

Use the steps below for self-installation, or proceed directly to guided setup assistance.

Get Started

The Admin Panel is the core of MegaClassify. Complete these requirements before installation.

CodeCanyon Buyers

You must use this online guide together with the documentation included inside your CodeCanyon ZIP package.

docs.title: 1) Server Requirements
docs.text:
Recommended production stack:

  • Linux (Ubuntu 20.04+/AlmaLinux/RockyLinux)
  • cPanel/WHM access (or equivalent hosting control panel)
  • Nginx (recommended) or Apache
  • PHP 8.1+ with required extensions
  • MySQL 5.7+ or MariaDB 10.4+
  • Composer 2.x
  • Node.js (if frontend assets need rebuild)
  • Valid SSL certificate

docs.title: 2) Required PHP Extensions
docs.text:
Enable common Laravel extensions:

  • bcmath
  • ctype
  • fileinfo
  • json
  • mbstring
  • openssl
  • pdo
  • pdo_mysql
  • tokenizer
  • xml
  • curl
  • zip
  • gd

docs.title: 3) Domain & DNS
docs.text:
Prepare:

  • Admin domain/subdomain (example: admin.example.com)
  • API endpoint domain if separated
  • DNS A record pointing to server IP
  • SSL certificate issuance readiness (AutoSSL/Let's Encrypt in cPanel)

docs.title: 4) Database Preparation
docs.text:
Create a dedicated database and user:

  • Database Name: {{DB_NAME}}
  • Username: {{DB_USER}}
  • Password: {{DB_PASSWORD}}
  • Host: 127.0.0.1 (or managed DB host)

Grant full privileges for this DB user on the created DB.

docs.title: 5) Buyer Verification Checklist (Pre-Install)
docs.text:
• [ ] Valid purchase code available
  • [ ] CodeCanyon buyer account details verified
  • [ ] CodeCanyon ZIP downloaded and extracted
  • [ ] Included offline documentation reviewed
  • [ ] Deployment target domain ready

docs.title: 6) Folder Ownership & Permissions Strategy
docs.text:
For cPanel hosting, keep Laravel writable directories accessible to the account user and web server process:

find /home/{{CPANEL_USER}}/{{APP_PATH}} -type f -exec chmod 644 {} \;
find /home/{{CPANEL_USER}}/{{APP_PATH}} -type d -exec chmod 755 {} \;
chmod -R 775 /home/{{CPANEL_USER}}/{{APP_PATH}}/storage
chmod -R 775 /home/{{CPANEL_USER}}/{{APP_PATH}}/bootstrap/cache

Avoid 777 in production.

docs.title: Setup Mobile Application - Prerequisite
docs.text: Before starting installation, make sure you have all required tools, accounts, and values ready.

docs.title: 1) Required Tools
docs.text:
• Latest MegaClassify mobile source code ZIP from CodeCanyon
  • Flutter SDK
  • Recommended: 3.22.x
  • Minimum: 3.16+
  • Android Studio + Android SDK
  • Java (required for Android builds)
  • Xcode (for iOS build, macOS only)

docs.title: 2) Required Accounts
docs.text:
• Firebase account (for Android app registration and google-services.json)
  • Google account (for Google Maps/Places API key if used)
  • Play Console account (for Android release publishing)
  • Apple Developer account (for iOS release publishing)

docs.title: 3) Required Project Inputs
docs.text: Keep these values prepared before installation:

docs.title: App identity
docs.text:
• App name (display name)
  • Android package name (example: com.example.megaclassify)
  • iOS bundle ID (example: com.example.megaclassify)

docs.title: Backend and URLs
docs.text:
• API host URL (example: https://api.example.com)
  • Frontend URL (example: https://app.example.com)

docs.title: API keys
docs.text:
• Google Maps API key
  • Google Places API key

docs.title: Android release signing
docs.text:
• Keystore file (.jks) for release build
  • key.properties values:
  • storePassword
  • keyPassword
  • keyAlias
  • storeFile

docs.title: 4) Pre-check Commands
docs.text:
Run these before setup:

flutter --version
flutter doctor

Fix any issues shown by flutter doctor before moving to the installation steps.

docs.title: Setup Mobile Application - Installation Steps
docs.text: This page provides a clear, step-by-step installation flow for the MegaClassify mobile app.

docs.title: 1) Unzip and Open the Project
docs.text:
1. Unzip the downloaded mobile app source package.
  2. Open the project folder in your editor/IDE.

docs.title: 2) Run Initial Flutter Commands
docs.text:
From the project root, run:

flutter clean
flutter pub get

docs.title: 3) Create Firebase Project and Download JSON
docs.text:
1. Open Firebase Console.
  2. Create a new project.
  3. Add an Android app inside Firebase.
  4. Enter your Android package name and app name.
  5. Generate and download google-services.json.

docs.title: 4) Place Firebase File in App
docs.text:
Copy the downloaded file to:

  • android/app/google-services.json

docs.title: 5) Update Android App Identity and Keys
docs.text:
Open android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml and verify/update:

  • Package name
  • App label (app name)
  • Google Maps API key (meta-data entry, if used)

docs.title: 6) Update App Icon / Logo
docs.text:
Replace app launcher icons in the Android resources icon folders.

Common locations include:

  • android/app/src/main/res/mipmap-*
  • Any project-specific icon/logo assets folder used by your app

docs.title: 7) Generate Android Keystore (Release)
docs.text:
Create a release keystore file and keep it inside:

  • android/keystore/

Example command:

keytool -genkey -v -keystore android/keystore/release-key.jks -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 10000 -alias release

docs.title: 8) Configure key.properties
docs.text:
Create or update android/key.properties:

storePassword=YOUR_STORE_PASSWORD
keyPassword=YOUR_KEY_PASSWORD
keyAlias=release
storeFile=keystore/release-key.jks

docs.title: 9) Update App Config Values
docs.text:
Open:

  • lib/core/config/app_config.dart

Update the following values:

  • Host URL (API base URL)
  • Frontend URL
  • Google Places API key

docs.title: 10) Build the App
docs.text:
After configuration is complete, build APK/AAB:

flutter build apk
# or
flutter build appbundle

docs.title: Quick Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] flutter clean and flutter pub get completed
  • [ ] Firebase project created
  • [ ] google-services.json placed in android/app/
  • [ ] Manifest package name, app label, and Maps API key updated
  • [ ] App icons/logo replaced
  • [ ] Keystore generated in android/keystore/
  • [ ] android/key.properties updated
  • [ ] lib/core/config/app_config.dart updated
  • [ ] Release build generated successfully

docs.title: 1) Configure Environment (React/Vite)
docs.text:
Set production values in your frontend environment file (example: .env.production):

VITE_APP_NAME=MegaClassify
VITE_API_BASE_URL=https://apimega.megzed.com

Also configure branding keys and analytics IDs if your build uses them.

docs.title: 2) Install and Build (React/Vite)
docs.text:
From web source directory:

npm install
npm run build

Build output is typically generated in dist/.

docs.title: 3) Deploy Build Output to Web Server
docs.text:
• Upload dist/ contents to your frontend domain document root
  • If hosted in cPanel, use File Manager or Git deployment
  • Configure SPA fallback so unknown routes return index.html
  • Ensure HTTPS is enabled

docs.title: Nginx SPA Fallback Example
docs.text:
location / {
  try_files $uri $uri/ /index.html;
}

docs.title: Apache (.htaccess) SPA Fallback Example
docs.text:
<IfModule mod_rewrite.c>
  RewriteEngine On
  RewriteBase /
  RewriteRule ^index\.html$ - [L]
  RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-f
  RewriteCond %{REQUEST_FILENAME} !-d
  RewriteRule . /index.html [L]
</IfModule>

docs.title: 4) Post-Deploy Validation
docs.text:
• Open homepage and listing pages
  • Verify login/register actions
  • Confirm API data loads without CORS errors
  • Refresh direct route URLs (for example /profile or /listing/123) to validate SPA fallback

docs.title: Blank Page After Deploy
docs.text:
• Check browser console for missing asset paths
  • Verify Vite base setting and deployment path
  • Confirm dist/assets/* files are uploaded

docs.title: CORS Error on API Calls
docs.text:
• Allow frontend domain in backend CORS config
  • Ensure preflight OPTIONS requests are handled

docs.title: 404 on Refresh (SPA Routes)
docs.text:
• Web server fallback rule is missing or incorrect
  • Re-check Nginx/Apache rewrite config

docs.title: Setup Web Application - Prerequisite
docs.text:
Before deploying the web application, ensure:

  • Admin/API backend is fully installed and reachable
  • Correct API base URL is available
  • Domain and SSL are ready for web frontend
  • React/Vite build environment (Node.js + npm) is installed

docs.title: Buyer Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Read web setup guide from CodeCanyon ZIP
  • [ ] Confirm API health endpoints are reachable
  • [ ] Confirm CORS and HTTPS policies are ready
